related_questions.question: How much does arthritis surgery cost?

text_blocks.snippet: The cost of arthritis surgery varies widely, depending on the type of surgery, the joint involved, the location of the surgery, and insurance coverage. Knee and hip replacement surgeries can range from $20,000 to $112,000 or more, while smaller procedures like those for thumb arthritis can cost between $3,000 and $7,000.
snippet_highlighted_words: Knee and hip replacement surgeries can range from $20,000 to $112,000 or more, while smaller procedures like those for thumb arthritis can cost between $3,000 and $7,000

list.title: Type of Surgery:
list.snippet: Total joint replacements (like knee or hip) are generally more expensive than partial replacements or arthroscopic procedures.

list.title: Joint Involved:
list.snippet: Knee and hip replacements are common, while procedures on smaller joints like the thumb or ankle may have different cost ranges.

list.title: Surgical Technique:
list.snippet: Robotic-assisted surgery or minimally invasive techniques can sometimes increase costs.

list.title: Location of Surgery:
list.snippet: Costs can vary by state, hospital, and even between academic and private centers.

list.title: Insurance Coverage:
list.snippet: Most insurance plans cover joint replacement surgery, but the out-of-pocket costs can vary significantly based on your deductible, copays, and coinsurance.

list.title: Pre- and Post-operative Care:
list.snippet: Costs include pre-surgery doctor visits, lab work, anesthesia, hospital stay, and post-surgery physical therapy or rehabilitation.

list.title: Implants:
list.snippet: The cost of the implant itself can be a significant factor, especially in total joint replacements.

list.title: Surgeon's Fees:
list.snippet: Surgeon fees can vary based on their experience and the complexity of the procedure.
Knee Replacement: $20,000 to $112,000 for total knee replacement; $14,188 to $49,016 or more for a partial knee replacement.
Hip Replacement: $19,476 to $30,700 (inpatient) or around $22,078 (outpatient), according to GoodRx.
Talk to your doctor and insurance provider: Get an accurate estimate of costs and discuss your options for managing expenses.
Consider outpatient surgery: If appropriate, outpatient procedures can be more affordable.
Look into financing options: Some hospitals offer financing or payment plans.
Explore post-surgery rehabilitation: Outpatient physical therapy may be less expensive than inpatient rehabilitation.
Be aware of potential hidden costs: Factor in potential expenses for medications, assistive devices, or complications.
